prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Houston, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1216; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped in the right lane of a northbound arterial road in Houston, Texas, when the rear of the vehicle was struck by Driver 2, whose car had been following closely behind. Driver 1 reported pain in the lower back shortly after the impact and said the seat had pushed forward sharply on contact, a sequence that fits the reported injury for a collision of this type. A Passenger was also seated in the front of Driver 1's vehicle and was identified by responding officers and by the statements of several bystanders who saw the impact. Driver 2 acknowledged that he failed to stop in time and did not dispute the sequence of events. Independent witnesses, scene photographs, and Driver 2's own account all agree that the collision happened as described. The rear bumper damage and the crumpled trunk lid are largely consistent with the force of the impact. A few older scratches on the lower rear panel may predate this crash and were noted separately. Records show Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering the vehicle involved. No citations were issued at the scene, and the officer completed the report after a brief inspection of both vehicles.
